recordedOn: Apple M4 Max, macOS 26.5.2, Node 22.23.1 (the flake devShell's node — the version CI runs; recorded with `nix develop --command pnpm bench --update-baseline`). Each figure is the median of FIVE whole-benchmark runs, not one. RECORDED UNDER CONCURRENT LOAD: see the spread figures in the note, which are three to five times wider than the previous recording's and are the machine, not the code.
note: guards are slow/fast A/B ratios measured in one process against one data set: the machine cancels, so these are the real gate (tolerance 1.30, except the shipped-vs-frozen gate at 1.15). workloads are workload/yardstick ratios and are only approximately machine-independent — indicative, not authoritative (tolerance 2.0). WHAT MOVED IN THIS RECORDING, AND WHY: greedy meshing landed (domain/mesh.ts). `meshChunk/*` fell to 0.37-0.45x of the previous figures because `meshChunk` is now the merging mesher and skips the air column above the terrain (`solidCeiling`); the previous figures were the naive full-height mesher, which is now `meshChunkNaive/*` and is recorded here for the first time. Comparing `meshChunk/*` against `meshChunkNaive/*` OVERSTATES the merge: measured with the Y-scan ceiling forced off, the merge alone is 1.16-1.47x SLOWER than naive on every shape, worst on checkerboard, and the whole wall-clock win is the ceiling. See docs/design-notes.md M-9. `simplifyMesh/*` fell by two to three orders of magnitude on flat and layered, and by 7.6x on rolling, for a different reason entirely: it is not faster, it is being handed a far smaller mesh (flat 4608 -> 10 quads). checkerboard-worst barely moved (23.08 -> 21.8) because nothing merges there. ON SPREAD: observed across the five recording runs, guards 5.9-9.1% except neighbour-read/shipped-vs-frozen-inline-reference at 23.2% and neighbour-read/option-vs-plain-number at 21.3%; workloads 34-66%. The previous recording saw 3-8% and 6-10%. The difference is concurrent load on the recording machine, not a change in the code, and it means the WORKLOAD figures here should be treated as weaker than usual — the 2.0 tolerance absorbs it, but a run that lands just inside the gate is not evidence of anything. The guard figures are unaffected in the way that matters: they are A/B ratios in one process, and all five are within 8% of the previous recording. ON NODE VERSIONS: the same benchmark on Node 24.13.0 puts the workload ratios well above these. The recorded environment is Node 22; comparing across major versions is not meaningful.
